evidence.note: Agent surveys all three test suites and counts feature scope (146 c-testsuite, 221 wacc, 413 gcc-torture), showing a rough mental list of required C features, but never converts this into an ordered sequence of feature milestones with per-stage success checks.

Commits to writing the entire compiler (lexer, preprocessor, AST, parser, codegen) into one monolithic main.rs before any compilation or test run. Stage labels are pipeline components, not verifiable language-feature milestones (no 'get return-int compiling, then expressions').

The whole back half is consumed by getting the single monolithic file to compile (brace-balance/heredoc struggles). No milestone is ever closed against a test subset; run_tests.sh is read at step 2 but never executed anywhere in the trajectory.

reasoning: The agent attempts the whole language in one monolithic push rather than a dependency-ordered feature progression, placing it near anchor 0. It is lifted slightly by having a rough feature inventory (from test scanning) and a component-level pipeline ordering, but there is no sequencing tied to feature dependencies and no per-milestone done-signal via test subsets—the suite is never even run. This matches the low end of the scale, between anchors 0 and 3, at 2.
